title: What's new in v2.10.0
summary: Threat Intelligence goes from watching to blocking: a Web Application Firewall for your self-hosted apps, and Automatic Blocking on your gateway, the WAF, and Cloudflare.

steps.title: Web Application Firewall
steps.listLabel: Catch attacks hidden inside HTTPS with the companion reverse proxy
steps.body: See the probes and exploit attempts aimed at your self-hosted apps, which a gateway's IPS can't read inside HTTPS. It runs in **NetworkOptimizer-Proxy**, the companion Traefik reverse proxy: turn on its **netopt-waf**, clear false positives with **Add Exclusion**, then switch from Detection Only to **Block**.

steps.title: Protection Setup
steps.listLabel: Go from watching attacks to blocking them, one step at a time
steps.body:
Each row shows where this site stands and the one action that finishes it, and **Turn On Recommended** does most of it in one click. **Trusted Sources** keeps your sites' own addresses from ever being blocked, and keeps UniFi Network Lists of them current, so a port forward can admit only your other sites as their WAN addresses change.

The **Blocking** tab lists every source blocked, each linked to its details.

steps.title: Automatic Blocking
steps.listLabel: Block repeat attackers on your gateway, the WAF, and Cloudflare
steps.body: Four Public Block Lists, from Spamhaus, abuse.ch, DShield, and blocklist.de, block known-bad networks before they try, and can stop an infected device from reaching its botnet's command server. Start in **Detection Only** to see what would be blocked.

steps.title: WAN Flood Protection
steps.listLabel: Stop a flood from freezing the gateway
steps.body:
A flood aimed at your WAN address can max out one of the gateway's cores far below your line rate, stalling everything that shares it. UniFi has no rate limit for traffic to the gateway itself, and its IPS never sees it. The gateway's **On-Site Agent** limits new connections per source, then drops a flood's source before it reaches Smart Queues.

Replies to anything your network opened are never counted. **Turn On Recommended** includes it, or start in **Detection Only** to see what it would drop.

steps.title: Packet Loss in WAN Speed Test
steps.listLabel: Speed tests now measure packet loss, idle and under load
steps.body:
Every WAN speed test now measures packet loss with your line idle and while it's saturated in each direction. You'll see it next to the latency in **Latest Result**, and over time on the **Packet Loss** tab of **WAN History**.

When Monitoring sees enough other traffic on that WAN to explain a slow result, the test is marked **Invalid** and ISP Health leaves it out.

steps.title: Realtek ONT Stick, One Card
steps.listLabel: Merge your Realtek stick into its SFP port's card, with an alert if it hangs
steps.body: Attach your Realtek stick to its SFP port for one card with its PON state, OLT, uptime, and firmware, plus an alert if its page stops answering while the light stays on. **Edit** it here and pick the port under **Attach to SFP Module**.
